name: Shringar House of Mangalsutra Ltd
title: Shringar House of Mangalsutra Ltd - 544512 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 106.5% YoY to INR725.6 crore and FY26 PAT rose 89% to INR115.5 crore, with working capital absorbing cash.
summary.overview: Shringar reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR725.6 crore (+106.5% YoY) with PAT of INR34 crore (+123.5%), and FY26 revenue of INR2,245.8 crore (+57.1%) and PAT of INR115.5 crore (+89%). Production capacity was raised from 2,500 kg to 4,000 kg in Q4, with FY26 utilisation at 87% on a blended 2,625 kg. The company entered bridal jewellery with Tanishq and Malabar Gold and Diamonds, and management reiterated about 30% value CAGR guidance for the next two to three years. Management acknowledged that working capital growth absorbed cash, leaving free cash flow negative, and said it expects to shift toward outright sales and organised clients within about two quarters.

segments.name: Mangalsutra (core)
segments.commentary: About 70% of FY26 revenue from outright sales and 30% from job work per management; mangalsutra sales are guided up 33-35% within FY27. Corporate clients were 49% and non-corporate 51% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Job work revenue (labour fee) was INR28 crore in FY26 versus INR26 crore in FY25, per management.

segments.name: Bridal jewellery
segments.commentary: Launched in Q4 FY26; first lot delivered in May 2026 to Titan (Tanishq). Management expects bridal to be about one-third of revenue within FY27 and on par with mangalsutra in about three years, though contribution is currently small.

guidance_outlook: Value growth guidance of about 30% CAGR over the next two to three years, stated as a minimum target; management said it could exceed 30-35% if gold prices stay steady.
FY27 mangalsutra sales expected to rise about 33-35% within the year.
Volume growth of about 15% in FY26; management aims to sustain this and accelerate toward 30-35% if gold prices stay steady.
Expects to convert a significant portion of operations to outright sales and become cash-flow positive within roughly two quarters.
Installed capacity stays at 4,000 kg for FY27, with further ramp-up expected in coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Capacity expanded from 2,500 kg to 4,000 kg during Q4 FY26; blended FY26 capacity 2,625 kg with 87% utilisation.
Opened a new branch office in Pune to extend reach across Marathwada and Vidarbha.
Gold hedging: about 3.5 tonnes annual production; 30% barter (gold-to-gold, already hedged), 17% GML, 13% MCX hedged, roughly 60% hedge ratio.
Around 10 large exhibitions organised in the year, which raised advertising spend.
demand_pricing: Client base of 1,333 customers across India and abroad; management plans to shift weight toward organised players such as Tata, Birla, Reliance, Malabar, Joyalukkas, Kalyan and PNG.
Malabar Gold and Diamonds accounted for 17% of revenue; Titan is a job-work client, so management said its value is not comparable.
Average inventory cost of gold about INR10,500 per gram on weighted-average basis; management cited gold prices up nearly 2x YoY (INR1,52,228 as of 15 April 2026).
Management said April and May 2026 were not particularly difficult, with corporate orders continuing without interruption.
Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15%; management said the increase is absorbed into domestic gold prices and has not caused distinct difficulties.
Management cited about 1 crore weddings in FY26 and weddings growing about 7-8% annually.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital increase and the debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the debt-equity ratio is 0.27 and inventory churn is about five times; higher working capital was needed to support revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in other expenses in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to notional hedging losses on MCX-hedged gold, plus about 10 exhibitions, machinery and setup costs for the new factory, and higher CSR spend.

qa_highlights.question: What is the job work versus outright sales split and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 30% job work and 70% outright sales. Job work earned INR28 crore in FY26 as a labour fee. Management said converting job work to outright sales could lift revenue to INR70-80 crore on the same volume and triple profit on that volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital rise and was the cycle lengthening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outright sales require more capital, which is the trade-off for higher margin. It expects organised clients with fixed payment dates to ease cash-flow churn over time. It did not give debtor or inventory day figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% guidance value or volume growth, and does it include bridal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% guidance is value growth and a minimum target. Bridal is not included in that guidance; it could push growth above 30% if bridal reaches parity with mangalsutra within three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will free cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to convert a significant portion of operations to outright contracts within about two quarters, which should help move cash flow from negative to positive.

risks_watch: Negative free cash flow in Q4 FY26 driven by working capital; watch debtor and inventory days and whether cash flow turns positive in about two quarters.
Gold price volatility (near doubling YoY) and hedging losses; FY26 hedge ratio about 60%.
Shift from job work to outright sales raises capital needs and inventory risk, and depends on clients such as Tanishq converting contracts.
Q4 EBITDA margin fell 41 bps YoY despite higher gross margin, driven by hedging notional losses, exhibitions and CSR spend.
Bridal jewellery is at an early stage with a small contribution; the first lot was delivered in May 2026.
Management did not give a split of revenue by client beyond Malabar at 17%; client concentration remains unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and strategy, with specific targets, but cautious and at times vague on cash flow and working capital. Management avoided quantifying bridal contribution and client-level concentration beyond Malabar at 17%.
key_quotes: We remain committed to our guidance of delivering approximately 30% growth over the next two to three years.
Therefore, an outright sale is always more beneficial for us than undertaking job work.
Within approximately two quarters, we will have converted a significant portion of our operations.

adds.what: Production capacity raised from 2,500 kg to 4,000 kg during Q4 FY26 (expansion completed)

growth.why: Management reiterates about 30% value CAGR for FY27-FY29 and guides mangalsutra sales up 33-35% in FY27, backed by the completed 2,500 kg to 4,000 kg capacity expansion and bridal entry, but no order-book or contracted volumes were quantified and capacity stays flat at 4,000 kg for FY27.
